text, read as fences, not summarized from the revision-log prose above them), Examples of done, Relationship to
other work — then the full prior `AC Red-Team` history, with particular weight on re-verify 13 and re-verify 14,
to confirm this round is not re-litigating settled ground. No shell/diff tool was available in this environment
(`git status` at spawn showed a pending working-tree modification to this file, but no tool present could render
it); this pass reviews the file's live content directly, which is the authoritative current draft regardless of
how it got there.

### What round 23 got right, re-verified

The re-verify-14 finding is answered on its own terms: AC-7's marker is no longer per-derivation shape
(indistinguishable for the loose/data-flow pair, shared for three of six) but capability-level — use of the
`ast` module, read off parsed syntax (Import/ImportFrom node naming `ast`, or an Attribute node on the binding
such an import creates) and never off source text, which correctly avoids the self-match failure mode
(the check's own module necessarily carries the planted fixture's source as a string literal) that a
text-matching detector would fall into. Completeness is correctly moved to the one identity a scan can decide —
six named exports resolving to six distinct function objects — rather than left inside the now-abandoned
per-derivation cardinality. The two live verifications the fold's own narrative claims to have run (nothing
under `obsidian_schemas/` or `tests/` references `ast` today, so single-homing is satisfiable rather than red
on arrival; and the self-match exposure that forced the parsed-syntax-not-text clause) read consistent with the
check as specified. The Approach and Check-strategy note were also corrected to drop the retired per-derivation
vocabulary, closing the four-rounds-running "the Approach was left behind" defect.

### MATERIAL — AC-7's SUFFICIENCY claim is false for one of the six derivations it claims to cover: the file-set walk touches no syntax and never references `ast`

AC-7's `desc:` states the load-bearing premise the whole capability-detection mechanism rests on: *"every
private copy of ANY of the six shared derivations must traverse syntax it first obtains via `ast` (a copy that
never touches syntax derives nothing)."* That premise is asserted, not derived — and it is false for one of the
six derivations AC-2 enumerates and AC-7 itself names as its completeness set: **the file-set walk** ("every
`.py` under `obsidian_schemas/`, recursively, discovered on disk"). Walking a directory tree for `.py` files is
pure filesystem enumeration — `pathlib.Path.rglob("*.py")` or `os.walk` — and requires no syntax traversal and
no reference to `ast` at all. The Approach's own text keeps the two steps distinct: "an AST scan over a file
set the test itself WALKS" names the walk and the scan as separate operations, and only the second one touches
syntax. A private, duplicated copy of *just* the file-set walk — the simplest and least syntactically-loaded of
the six named derivations, and therefore the one a builder is most likely to consider "too trivial to bother
importing for" — would not contain an `import ast` or any `ast.*` attribute anywhere, so AC-7's single-homing
scan would still find the marker in exactly one module (the real shared one) and read GREEN while a second,
divergent file-set walk exists in the tree.

This is not fully absorbed by AC-1/AC-2/AC-3/AC-5's own `__module__` self-cert clauses, which only catch a
private copy that is the literal binding *that specific test* invokes. AC-7 exists precisely for the
complementary case — Approach and AC-1's own text call it out: "AC-7 covers the complementary case of a second
definition site that exists whether or not this test uses it." A file-set-walk duplicate written for code the
self-certifying four tests never call — a sixth test added later (the Examples of done's own
`merge_frontmatter_field` scenario), a lint/CLI helper, or a seventh derivation a future round adds per AC-7's
own "extends this export list" allowance — is exactly the gap AC-7 is supposed to close and, for this one
derivation, structurally cannot.

**Concrete failure scenario.** A builder correctly implements all four consuming tests importing the shared
module's predicates (AC-1/2/3/5's self-cert clauses all pass). Later, someone adds a new test or a small helper
that needs "the list of `.py` files under `obsidian_schemas/`" and writes a private three-line
`Path("obsidian_schemas").rglob("*.py")` loop rather than importing the shared module for a directory listing —
plausibly the least-effort path, since it is fewer lines than the import plus the shared module's own signature.
That copy silently differs from the canonical walk (e.g. it does not filter `__pycache__`, or it is pointed at
the wrong root, or it misses a nested subpackage) — precisely the "two independently-written [things] that agree
on today's tree diverge on the first future case" scenario every other round in this arc exists to prevent —
and AC-7 does not fire, because the duplicate references no `ast` symbol anywhere.

**What would have to change.** AC-7's SUFFICIENCY clause needs to be honest per-member rather than blanket: five
of the six derivations (the two write-path predicates, the subclass scan, the MRO resolution, the closure
computation) genuinely cannot be computed without traversing parsed syntax, so capability-detection on `ast`
soundly covers them. The sixth, the file-set walk, needs either its own distinct marker (a capability every
implementation of *it* must exercise — e.g. `pathlib`/`os.walk`/`os.scandir` usage, single-homed the same way),
or an explicit statement that its uniqueness is carried entirely by AC-1/AC-2/AC-3/AC-5's own self-cert clauses
and is out of AC-7's scope for a stated reason — never left implied by a SUFFICIENCY sentence that, read
literally, claims a coverage it does not have. This is the document's own repeatedly-derived rule turned on
round 23's remedy: a scan's map — here, a capability's claimed coverage — cannot be keyed to a class its members
do not all exercise.

### What I attacked and found clean

- AC-7's parsed-syntax-vs-source-text distinction and the self-match failure mode it closes — re-read against
  the check's own necessary structure (it must write the plant's source somewhere) — hold.
- The two planted-negative marker forms (bare `import ast`; an `ast.*` attribute reference reached through a
  from-import or an aliased import) are each independently matched by the stated marker definition (an
  Import/ImportFrom node naming `ast` fires on the import line itself regardless of how the imported name is
  later referenced), so the planted-negative clause is sound for the forms it names.
- Completeness-by-name (six exports resolving to six distinct function objects) is a sound, decidable property
  independent of the SUFFICIENCY gap above — it is not affected by this finding and does not need to change.
- Re-checked AC-1/AC-3/AC-5's `__module__` self-cert clauses against the current text — each explicitly lists
  the file-set walk among the callables it certifies, so the gap here is scoped to a duplicate NOT invoked by
  one of those four tests, not to a regression in what they already cover.
- Re-checked the specification-altitude declaration (line 483): this finding is a derivation-obligation
  completeness gap — item (b) — not a harness-factoring or internal-unit-testing concern, so it sits on the
  declared floor and is not routed away, consistent with how rounds 20–23's findings at this same altitude were
  treated.
- No regression found in AC-1 through AC-6's substantive content, the 4×3 matrix, the CLOSURE/PARTITION
  machinery, or the Examples of done — all read unchanged and consistent with the round-23 narrative's claims
  about what it did and did not touch.

### CRITICAL — AC-5's cross-repo consumer audit is unverifiable by its own named check

AC-5 requires "the three consumer call sites (enricher/introducer/scheduler) are audited so the return-contract change breaks none of them silently," bundled into the single check `test_write_paths_distinguish_failure_from_noop`. I confirmed HAL9000 is not present in this tree (`Glob **/HAL9000/**` → no files found) — the enricher, introducer, and scheduler consumers live entirely in other repositories (HAL9000, per this project's own README "Used By" table and CLAUDE.md). `obsidian-schemas`' hermetic test floor (`.venv/bin/python -m pytest .../tests`) cannot import or exercise code in those repos.

**Concrete failure scenario:** a builder writes `test_write_paths_distinguish_failure_from_noop` against `obsidian_schemas`' own functions only (proving `append_to_body_section` now raises on I/O failure and stays falsy-but-distinct on dedup), ticks AC-5 green, and never opens HAL9000's enricher/introducer/scheduler source. Those three call sites still do `if not repo.append_to_body_section(...): <treat as dedup>` (per the Constraints section's own description of today's pattern) — and now a genuine disk-full raises an uncaught exception up through code that was written to treat any falsy return as a benign no-op. The "audit" — the one thing the doc calls out as this finding's differentiator from the other four ("the only finding that is not purely internal") — has no mechanism in the AC set that forces it to happen, let alone verifiably.

**What would have to change:** either (a) split the audit into its own AC with its own check that names a verifiable artifact — e.g. a written record of each of the three call sites with file:line and the before/after behavior, checked by a `kind: command` grep/lint rather than a local pytest test — or (b) if HAL9000 is a golden dependency reachable in the build environment, the check must actually import and exercise those three call sites (an un-stubbed integration per spec-quality-bar Check 10's WI-050 clause, since the consumer breakage IS the thing under test here), not merely assert on `obsidian_schemas`' own local behavior.

### MATERIAL — AC-1 quantifies over three write paths but names one check with no coverage requirement

AC-1's desc: "When `update_fields`, `update_frontmatter_field`, **or** `update_frontmatter_fields` is called on a note whose frontmatter is malformed YAML, the call raises..." — three distinct functions, one check: `test_no_mutation_writes_through_failed_parse`. Nothing pins the test to exercise all three call paths.

**Concrete failure scenario:** a builder fixes and tests `update_fields` (base.py) against a malformed-YAML fixture, and the single named check passes. `update_frontmatter_field`/`update_frontmatter_fields` (writer.py:247-295, the sibling rebuild path the doc itself cites at line 26 as part of the SAME corruption chain) are left un-fixed and still do `parse_frontmatter → rebuild → write` on the silent `({}, content)` — AC-1 reads satisfied while two of its three named functions still corrupt notes. This is the WI-185/WI-131 pattern the gate is chartered to hunt: the property quantifies over a class of three call sites; a single hand-picked fixture/check closes it on paper only.

**What would have to change:** either split into per-function checks (or a parametrized single test asserting all three), or state explicitly in `check:` / `desc:` that the test must cover all three named functions.

### MATERIAL — AC-1/AC-2 have no covering case for "absent frontmatter must still succeed"

The Approach section states the fix must make "malformed" distinguishable from "genuinely absent" so write paths can tell them apart — but every AC in the set only tests the malformed-and-must-raise half. Nothing in AC-1 through AC-5 asserts that a write/mutate call on a note with genuinely absent frontmatter (the legitimate case, `parser.py:64-65`) still succeeds and creates frontmatter as today.

**Concrete failure scenario:** a builder implements the simplest thing that makes AC-1 and AC-2 pass — `parse_frontmatter` raises on ANY case where it can't hand back a "real" frontmatter dict, absent included, not just on `yaml.YAMLError`. AC-1's raise-and-untouched assertion is satisfied (arguably over-satisfied), AC-2's "distinguishable" claim could even be read as satisfied by the presence of a new exception type. But a legitimately frontmatter-less note now can never have frontmatter added via `update_fields`/`update_frontmatter_field(s)` — a real regression on ordinary note creation — and no AC in the set would catch it, because none tests the absent-frontmatter write path at all. This is the "absence, not a wrong assertion" class the gate's Step 3 calls out as the one a checklist misses.

**What would have to change:** add an explicit positive case (to AC-1 or AC-2) asserting a write/mutate call on a genuinely-frontmatter-less note still succeeds and produces the expected frontmatter — pinning the "absent ≠ malformed" distinction from both directions, not just the malformed side.

### MATERIAL — AC-3 conflates two distinct failure predicates under one fixture word, and folds an unrelated narrowing into the same check with no mechanism-forcing assertion

Two separate issues in one AC:

1. **"unparseable-or-invalid"** covers both C2/C4's predicate (YAML that fails to parse) and C5's predicate (YAML that parses fine but fails Pydantic validation for a *known* `type`) — the doc's own Exploration Notes treat these as two different sites (parser.py:78 vs parser.py:148) with two different corruption/duplication stories. 2. The person.py:1147-1160 narrowing (re-verified live: still a bare `except Exception: logger.debug(...)`) is folded into the same check (`test_batch_load_survives_and_surfaces_bad_notes`) with a success condition of "not swallowed to DEBUG" — which a builder satisfies by changing `logger.debug` to `logger.warning` on the existing bare `except Exception`, without narrowing the except clause to let a genuine `VaultPathNotConfiguredError` (or anything unexpected) actually surface as the Approach section recommends ("narrow the except to the expected-unavailable cases... and let anything else surface"). The doc's own A5 rejects exactly this move ("Logging... has never stopped anything") for the sibling C4 finding, but AC-3's literal wording doesn't rule it out here.

**What would have to change:** (1) require a second fixture in AC-3 (or a companion AC) using a schema-validation-failure note, not only a YAML-parse-failure note; (2) reword the person.py:1147-1160 clause to require the except clause itself narrows (e.g., asserted by a test that a `VaultPathNotConfiguredError` raised inside the try block propagates rather than being swallowed), not merely that the log level changed.
